issues.reason: The issue mistakes a coverage gap for a defect — it is the reviewer's own second gap ("no top-level handle on the rule-derived per-member event") — and the improvisation is graceful: (sk_file sk_lawsuit_1) is the instruction set's own Skolem-function term with its variable instantiated by the constant the rule's premise (PartOf sk_lawsuit_1 sk_group_1) supplies, so it denotes exactly the event the rule derives, and (Location ... pennsylvania) is true of the sentence and well-typed; the instruction set nowhere forbids a ground Skolem term, and the alternatives (a second sk_file_2 event, or LocatedIn on the lawsuit itself) each state something the sentence does not.

gaps_confirmed: exemplifying "including <NP>" naming one member of a just-introduced set — the participial rule routes drifted participles (concerning / regarding / following) to reduced relatives, which does not fit a set-exemplifier

attaching a modifier to one individuated member's own eventuality when only the group event plus the per-member distribution rule were emitted: the instruction set provides no top-level handle on the rule-derived per-member event
new_gaps: truth-value coordination between a conditionally derived event and an unconditional modifier on it: (Location (sk_file sk_lawsuit_1) pennsylvania) is asserted at 1.0 0.99 while the event term it modifies only comes into being when the 1.0 0.9 distribution rule fires, and no rule says how the two truth values relate

"one" as a member-selector inside an exemplifying phrase falls between one-anaphora (which mints a FRESH entity of the antecedent's class, unlinked) and a partitive subset member; nothing says which reading licenses the PartOf link into the group just minted
notes: The group + CardinalityAtLeast 5 + agentless-passive group event + per-member distribution rule follow the Cardinality templates exactly, as does typing the exemplified "one" and linking it with PartOf.
